content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer | Java, Spring Boot, Event-Driven Services

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7 years of experience building and operating production services in Java and Spring. Experienced in designing REST APIs, working with relational databases, tuning query performance, and developing event-driven integrations with Kafka and RabbitMQ. Hands-on with automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS EKS, and CI/CD pipelines. Fluent in English and Portuguese.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java (8–17), Kotlin (basic)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, REST, OpenAPI
Data and messaging: Oracle, PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and delivery: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins
Testing and tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Lisbon
Jan 2022–Present
- Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed and versioned the REST API for a partner quoting integration used by 12 broker partners, using OpenAPI.
- Produce and consume Kafka events for the claims workflow; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table, removing duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 ms by adding Redis caching and resolving JPA N+1 queries.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes (EKS) using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in an on-call rota one week per month.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A. | Porto
Sep 2019–Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Contributed to monolith decomposition by extracting the notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-time) | CodeFarol Lda | Porto
Jul 2018–Aug 2019
- Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018

LANGUAGES
English (fluent) | Portuguese (fluent) | Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, concise, professionally structured CV with clear progression from junior developer to backend engineer. The summary is targeted to backend services, Java/Spring, REST APIs, relational databases, event-driven integration, containers, Kubernetes, AWS, testing, and CI/CD. The experience bullets are particularly effective because they include credible scope and measurable outcomes, such as seven microservices, 12 broker partners, reduction of p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, and increased test coverage from 35% to 70%. The document is truthful against the Original Candidate Information; no unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected. The main content limitation is that Python, schema migrations, REST API consumption, observability, and logistics experience are not evidenced, but these are candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard, ATS-readable headings, conventional reverse chronology, simple text formatting, explicit technologies, and strong keyword coverage for Java, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, EKS, AWS, automated testing, and Jenkins. It should parse reliably and has a high AI-screening probability for the job's comparable-language pathway. Screening probability will be lower in Python-first systems because Python and FastAPI do not appear, although the advertisement explicitly accepts Java as a comparable language. The CV also does not explicitly contain the phrases 'schema migrations' or 'REST API consumption'; these should not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the comparable Java pathway. The CV clearly shows seven years of backend development, production microservices, REST API design and versioning, relational database work, PostgreSQL in the skills inventory, query-performance improvement, Docker, AWS/EKS deployment, Kubernetes, Kafka, automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and on-call ownership. Fluent English is explicitly shown, and the technical decisions described—idempotent consumers, an outbox table, Redis caching, and resolving JPA N+1 queries—provide evidence of practical reliability and trade-off awareness. Gaps in the candidate material are professional Python/FastAPI experience, explicit willingness to work mainly in Python, schema migrations, explicit REST API consumption, observability tooling, logistics or EDI knowledge, Terraform, and Dutch or French. The document also does not explicitly show code review, design notes, incident post-mortems, or blameless post-mortems. These are alignment gaps, not defects that can be corrected without adding unsupported claims.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/positioning enhancement: In the Professional Summary section, change 'Experienced in designing REST APIs, working with relational databases, tuning query performance, and developing event-driven integrations with Kafka and RabbitMQ.' to 'Experienced in designing REST APIs, working with relational databases, tuning query performance, and building event-driven backend services with Kafka and RabbitMQ.' This uses the role's backend-services terminology while remaining fully supported by the experience section.

MINOR keyword enhancement: In the Technical Skills section, change the heading 'Cloud and delivery' to 'Cloud, Containers and CI/CD' and retain the existing technologies beneath it: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, and Jenkins. This makes the job's CI/CD and container keywords easier for ATS systems to associate with the relevant skills group without adding any unsupported technology.
